scope: Real Chicago skyline landmarks that can fall inside the proposed Railyards outfield sightline. The AECOM future-development masses are excluded.

coordinate_frame.axes: X east, Y north, Z up
coordinate_frame.projection: local tangent approximation at latitude 41.8645; x = delta-longitude * 111320*cos(latitude) plus home offset, y = delta-latitude * 110900 plus home offset
coordinate_frame.registration_note: The shared scene records an inferred +33 m X adjustment to align the rendering-derived field with the mapped river. These skyline XY values use the same frame and inherit the site-plan registration uncertainty (about 4-5 m at anchors), not survey coordinates.

outfield_geometry.interpretation: Home plate is [0,0] in the metric model; first base is +X and third base is +Y. Greater local azimuth is toward left field.

home_plate.occlusion: The current upper-bowl roof and outfield screens dominate the low field-eye view. Treat skyline visibility as upper silhouettes only until a roof/opening line-of-sight check is made.

home_upper_deck.occlusion: Upper-deck view should expose tower crowns above the 46-48 m canopy; the lower bowl, scoreboards and nearby proposed masses can hide bases.

third_base_seats.occlusion: This right-field-oriented bowl view does not frame the downtown cluster; use it as a negative visibility check.

buildings.name: The St. Regis Chicago

home_plate.expected: upper crown only; lower massing roof-occluded

buildings.visibility_reasoning: Nearest of the defining lakefront supertalls in the center-field/right-center window. Its 3-stem profile rises well above the canopy from the upper deck, while a field-eye view will lose the base.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Three offset, stacked frustum stems with different roof heights; blue-gray glass, visible slab-band rhythm, stepped/wavy profile. Keep the three tops separate rather than one rectangular tower.

buildings.name: Aqua
buildings.visibility_reasoning: Directly behind the proposed outfield cluster, slightly left of the St. Regis and close enough to read its irregular edge. Lower floors are hidden by the bowl from field level.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Tall blue-gray residential shaft with broad, irregular horizontal balcony plates that undulate beyond the core; use a soft light facade and dark inter-floor bands, no antenna.

buildings.name: Aon Center
buildings.height_source: Aon Center official facts: 1,136 ft; CTBUH tip 362.5 m
buildings.visibility_reasoning: Aon is a clean, high-contrast rectangular mass in the same east-northeast cluster as Aqua and Two Prudential. Its simple top remains readable even when the lower city is occluded.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Single monolithic pale/white granite rectangular prism, subtly tapered, with fine dark vertical window grid and flat roof. Avoid a decorative crown; the plain block is the identifier.

buildings.name: Two Prudential Plaza
buildings.visibility_reasoning: The east-northeast tower pair sits just beyond center field and is within both proposed home views. The nearby One Prudential Plaza should be modeled as a shorter companion mass.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Warm gray/gold rectangular shaft with strong vertical striping and a stepped postmodern crown/chevron profile. Pair it with One Prudential as a lower, squarer neighbor.

buildings.name: Trump International Hotel & Tower Chicago
buildings.height_source: CTBUH/Skyscraper Center, 423.2 m / 1,389 ft to architectural top

home_plate.expected: tall tapered shaft; lower half occluded

buildings.visibility_reasoning: Trump is farther toward left field than the Pru/Aon cluster but remains inside both home frustums. Its tall, tapered profile should read above the canopy despite distance.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Dark blue-gray glass shaft with setbacks near the top and a narrow white/gray spire; preserve the taper and spire, avoid a generic box.

buildings.name: 875 North Michigan Avenue
buildings.height_source: CTBUH/Skyscraper Center, 343.7 m architectural / 456.9 m to tip

home_plate.expected: distant X-braced shaft and antenna tips

buildings.visibility_reasoning: It is farther north than Trump but nearly the same outfield azimuth. Distance reduces apparent width; the antenna tips and external X braces are the useful identifiers.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Dark bronze/black rectangular shaft with bold external diagonal X-bracing on all faces, two slender antenna masts, and a slightly tapered crown.

buildings.name: One Prudential Plaza

home_upper_deck.expected: short companion block below Two Pru

buildings.visibility_reasoning: It shares the Pru cluster and occupies almost the same azimuth as Two Prudential Plaza. Include only as a supporting lower mass; the taller Two Pru carries the silhouette.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Shorter pale/gray rectangular office block with a clean flat top, narrow vertical window bands, and an understated rooftop element. Keep it subordinate to Two Pru.

buildings.name: Tribune Tower
buildings.height_source: OSM building footprint plus conservative architectural-height reference; use as approximate low-rise skyline mass

home_upper_deck.expected: small Gothic crown if gap remains

buildings.visibility_reasoning: The tower is a defining Chicago landmark but low relative to the surrounding supertalls. It belongs in the skyline layer only if a gap between Trump/875 and the Pru cluster remains.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Pale limestone neo-Gothic tower with a steep, crenellated crown, flying-buttress-like vertical edges, and a small central spire. Use low contrast and let taller buildings occlude its base.

buildings.name: Wrigley Building
buildings.height_source: OSM building levels/footprint proxy; approximate low-rise silhouette height
buildings.visibility_reasoning: Iconic but short and nearly aligned with Tribune/Trump. Treat as an optional historic crown; do not create a full downtown block around it.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Two pale terra-cotta towers with ornate clock crowns, one taller than the other, warm ivory lighting, and a narrow central separation.

buildings.name: Marina City
buildings.height_source: CTBUH/Skyscraper Center, 179.2 m / 588 ft for each twin tower

home_upper_deck.expected: twin cylindrical crown near frame edge

buildings.visibility_reasoning: Its twin cylindrical forms sit near the left side of the home frustums and are much more recognizable than their height suggests. Keep them at the edge of the upper-deck skyline.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Two identical cylindrical concrete towers with rounded balcony rings, dark central cores, and open circular parking decks; separate the twins visibly.

buildings.name: Willis Tower
buildings.height_source: Willis Tower official site: 1,450 ft; CTBUH/Skyscraper Center: 442.1 m architectural / 527 m antenna tip
buildings.visibility_reasoning: Do not assume Willis/Sears Tower is visible beyond center field. In the shared frame it lies almost due north at the left-field foul-line azimuth, about 36-37 degrees left of the center-field heading. It falls outside both supplied home-oriented horizontal frustums and would need an explicitly wider/panned left-field camera; nearby bowl/scoreboard geometry would also compete with its base.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Only add as a conditional left-field landmark: black bundled-tube stepped massing with major setbacks and two antenna masts. Keep it disabled for the supplied home-plate and home-upper-deck cameras unless the camera is widened or panned.

buildings.name: Salesforce Tower Chicago
buildings.height_source: Salesforce official media collection, 813 ft / 57 stories; CTBUH lists 255 m
buildings.visibility_reasoning: This real tower is west/northwest of the site, beyond the left-field edge of both home frustums. It belongs in a wider left-field skyline preset, not the default outfield backdrop.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Tall dark glass rectangular shaft with a crisp stepped/angled crown and narrow vertical emphasis; use as a low-detail far-left mass only.

buildings.name: River Point
buildings.height_source: River Point official site: 52 stories; CTBUH 222-223 m reference
buildings.visibility_reasoning: River Point is close geographically but sits northwest of the left-field foul direction, so proximity does not make it visible in the supplied home views. Reserve for a panned left-field or bridge view.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Blue-green glass shaft with a distinctive broad triangular/green roof cap and a narrow base; low-detail conditional mass.

buildings.name: 150 North Riverside
buildings.height_source: OSM building tag height=229 m; architect/developer confirms 54 stories
buildings.visibility_reasoning: A real and distinctive tower, but its local azimuth is just beyond left-field north and outside the home views. Its narrow base makes it easy to omit from the default skyline without changing the recognizable center-field cluster.
buildings.silhouette_modeling: Very slender glass tower with a small ground footprint and dramatic cantilevered upper body; use a narrow vertical blade with a broader top mass in a conditional left-field preset.
